paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: everything Jerusalem had, God gave her. He found her thrown out in an open field, lying in her blood, and He said, "Live!" (Ezekiel 16:6). The crown, the fame, the fine flour, honey and oil all came from Him. Verse 14 says her beauty was perfect "in the splendor I bestowed on you."

So what went wrong? She "trusted in your beauty" (Ezekiel 16:15) and used God's gifts to chase other things, and verse 22 says she "did not remember the days of your youth." When you forget where your gifts came from, you start thinking you made them, and a gift you think you earned ends up on the wrong altar. I know a little about remembering, though: I was a quarter stamper in a bin, and I did NOT forget who picked me up.

The passage is heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't, because God pledged Himself to her in a covenant (Ezekiel 16:8), and she gave His own children to idols (Ezekiel 16:20-21). His anger is real, and so is what follows: He says, "I will bring upon you the wrath of your bloodshed and jealousy" (Ezekiel 16:38), and her lovers strip her, tear down her shrines, and a mob stones her and burns her houses (Ezekiel 16:39-41). So here's your takeaway, baker: remember where you started and who called you, and let it keep your heart at home with Him. God isn't done speaking to Jerusalem yet, either.
